holod_dan.instruct: Man in his early thirties, hushed low voice close to the microphone, tense and frightened but controlled, breathy, slow careful delivery, American English, found-footage horror narrator speaking quietly at night so nobody wakes up.
holod_dan.ref: Okay. It's three in the morning. I'm going to walk down the hallway now. Just... stay quiet.

holod_jess.instruct: Young woman around thirty, just woke up, sleepy, scared trembling whisper, American English, quiet and fragile.
holod_jess.ref: Hello? Is somebody there? Please... I can hear you breathing.

lines.text: Never point a thermal camera at a mirror.
Every night at 3:14, my dog growls at the hallway.
lines.say: Every night at three fourteen, my dog growls at the hallway.

lines.text: It sees heat. Anything alive glows.
And glass doesn't let heat through. It bounces it back. Like a mirror.
The hallway was freezing. Someone had been touching the walls.
Jess was asleep. My side of the bed... was cold.
Then I saw it. At the end of the hall.
It didn't move. Until I did.
Then I remembered. Glass bounces heat.
Biscuit was never growling at the hallway.
